record.original_question: Does there exist, in ZFC, a set of reals with the Menger property U_fin(O, O) but without the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 5.1 ([24, Problem 3], [14, Problem 1], [12, Problem 1]). Does there exist (in ZFC) a set of reals X which has the Menger property Ufin(O, O) but not the Hurewicz property Ufin(O, Γ)?

Notes added in proof. Zdomskyy, in a series of recent works, settled (or partially settled) some of the problems mentioned in the paper, the answers being: “Yes” for Problem 5.1, “No” for Problem 8.6, and “Consistently yes” for Problem 11.2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an open cover U of a topological space X, recall the selection principle U_fin(O, O): X has this property (the Menger property) if for every sequence (U_n) of open covers of X there exist finite subfamilies F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃_n F_n is a cover of X. The space X has the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ) if, moreover, the finite subfamilies F_n can be chosen so that the sets V_n := ⋃ F_n form a γ-cover, i.e., every point x ∈ X belongs to V_n for all but finitely many n (equivalently, {V_n : n ∈ ω} is eventually a cover at every point).

Working in ZFC alone (without additional set-theoretic axioms beyond ZFC), does there exist a set of real numbers X ⊆ ℝ that has the Menger property U_fin(O, O) but does not have the Hurewicz property U_fin(O, Γ)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved in the affirmative by Tsaban and Zdomskyy ("Scales, fields, and a problem of Hurewicz", J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2008), who constructed in ZFC a set of reals that is Menger but not Hurewicz, providing a uniform (non-dichotomic) solution to Hurewicz's 1927 question.

status_evidence.title: Scales, fields, and a problem of Hurewicz
status_evidence.snippet: Tsaban and Zdomskyy construct in ZFC a Menger set of reals that is not Hurewicz, settling the long-standing Hurewicz problem.
status_evidence.claim: There exists in ZFC a set of reals with the Menger property but not the Hurewicz property.

status_evidence.title: Hurewicz space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Tsaban and Zdomskyy gave a uniform example of a Menger subset of the real line that is not Hurewicz, solving Hurewicz's problem in ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: ZFC example separating Menger from Hurewicz exists.
